records.text: The eyes can hold a position after a brief movement command has ended. An animal can also keep track of its location while the activity of individual neurons fluctuates. Both abilities require a useful quantity to remain represented in a changing biological system. The three papers study different parts of this problem: the loss of a stored value, the origin of slow eye motion, and the arrangement of spatial firing patterns.

records.purpose_and_order_reason: Holding eye position and keeping track of location motivate retaining a value despite changing cells; this introduces the shared question before neural terms.

records.text: The first distinction is between a value and the activity that represents it. Eye position is one number, but a circuit can represent it through thousands of neural activities. A disturbance can change those activities without changing the represented value. Another disturbance can leave a coherent activity pattern while changing the value. The geometry of these two changes will explain why a stable-looking circuit can still accumulate memory error.[^f-memory]

A [**firing rate**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} is the expected number of spikes per unit time. A rate of 20 hertz means an average of 20 spikes per second under the specified conditions, rather than a promise of one spike every 50 milliseconds.

records.text: Neurons affect one another through connections called [**synapse**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}s. In the models used here, an excitatory input increases a receiving neuron's tendency to fire and an inhibitory input reduces it. The effect of a spike can last beyond the spike itself because synaptic input decays over time. When neurons send signals back into the same population, the circuit has [**recurrent connectivity**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}. Such feedback can maintain activity after an external signal disappears.

records.text: A [**tuning curve**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} gives a neuron's expected firing rate as a function of a represented variable. The linear expression can describe an active range, but it must be modified where it would predict negative firing. The eye paper includes a firing threshold and terms for movement as well as position.[^f-eye]

records.text: Spatial tuning gives a second example. In the hippocampus, a brain structure involved in memory and navigation, a [**place cell**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} fires strongly in one or more localized regions of an environment. A connected region of elevated spatial firing is a [**place field**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}. One neuron can have several fields. A [**rate map**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} estimates the rate at each position by dividing the spikes recorded there by the time spent there. Sparse visits, smoothing, and firing cutoffs therefore affect the estimated map and its fields. A field in a model's expected rate and a field extracted from finite recordings are related objects with different measurement uncertainties.[^f-place]

records.text: For changing rates, the expected count is the integral $\lambda=\int r(t)\,dt$. In a recurrent network, $r(t)$ itself depends on past activity. It is stable in a direction if a small disturbance in that direction decays.

records.text: Memory of a continuous quantity calls for a family of persistent states. A [**continuous attractor**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} is a continuous family of fixed points with restoring dynamics toward the family and a neutral direction along it. Neutral means that there is no restoring force along that direction in the ideal deterministic model. The family is an [**attractor manifold**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}. Its dimension counts independent coordinates represented on it, rather than neurons in the circuit. A line attractor has one represented coordinate; a ring can represent a periodic coordinate such as heading.[^f-memory]

records.text: For state dependent $D$, where the coefficient is evaluated affects the process. With the same written coefficient and zero written drift, it describes a different process from the Itô equation. Converting the Stratonovich equation into Itô form adds a drift $D'/2$. records.text: With $D$ of order $1/N$, random displacement over $dt$ is of order $\sqrt{dt/N}$, while such a mean displacement is of order $dt/N$. records.text: The independence assumption also has a precise scope. Newly generated spike-count fluctuations are conditionally independent given the present state. Shared recurrent fluctuations can still correlate the observed spike trains over time. An extra source of correlated fluctuations would change the projection formula to $2D=\mathbf v^TQ\mathbf v$, where $Q\,dt$ is their increment covariance. Calculating the corresponding Fisher information would require the matching joint likelihood. The paper discusses such correlated models as future extensions ([Discussion, p. 5, paragraph beginning “Our spiking model”](../papers/burak-fiete-2012-persistent-activity.pdf#page=5&zoom=125,0,142)); it does not prove that every correlated spiking model obeys its Poisson formulas.[^p1-correlation]
